text:
irene: Heads-up: canary reranker v7-int8 shows NDCG stable (+0.1%) but MRR -2.6 on longtail cohort (cohort=lt-2025). Drop concentrated on queries with very few clicks (sparse qids) and on queries that rely on date tokens. Anyone seen similar?

zack: Can you paste the quick slice summary?

irene: quick summary + s3: s3://redwood-bench/rerank/3400012345/summary.csv
```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1,sample_size
float32,lt-2025,0.592,0.451,0.47,12000
int8,lt-2025,0.593,0.440,0.45,12000
float32,core-2025,0.633,0.512,0.54,30000
int8,core-2025,0.631,0.510,0.53,30000
```

meera: 2.6% MRR on longtail is worrying. Is the cohort mostly low-click queries where a single swap kills MRR? Need per-query disagreement dump and bootstrap CI.

irene: uploaded disagree_1000.jsonl with per-query top-5 and click labels. Link: s3://redwood-bench/rerank/3400012345/disagree_1000.jsonl

zack: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) quantization increases score noise and causes rank flips on low-signal queries, (2) sampling differences in the offline eval harness (we recently changed candidate sampler to stratify by doc_age) changed some candidate composition for lt queries. Which did canary run use?

irene: Canary used the same candidate job id but eval harness flag `candidate_sampler=age_stratified_v2` was enabled in float run and accidentally disabled in int8 run. I'm re-checking run metadata now.

meera: That alone could change recall for date-sensitive docs. But we also had the new per-layer PTQ scale clipping in int8 that slightly compresses logits; that could bias toward older docs if recency token embeddings quantize differently. So both plausible.

zack: Run plan: (A) int8 with float sampler (stratified on) to test candidate composition; (B) int8 mixed-last-layer; (C) float but with int8 scorer scaling to simulate clipping. Also compute bootstrap 95% CI on MRR for the longtail slice.

irene: Kicked off A/B/C on a 10k longtail subset. Jobs: 3400012355 (A), 3400012366 (B), 3400012377 (C). CI link: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/3400012355

eval-bot: Started bootstrapped CI job 3400012358 for lt-2025 (1000 resamples).

ci-bot: Jobs queued: 3400012355, 3400012366, 3400012377.

zack: Also request: per-query score distributions (float vs int8) for top-3 docs and delta histograms. If quant adds heavier tails we can see it.

irene: Uploaded sample histograms and one example case where float and int8 disagree on a query with date token "2021-07":
```
query: "what changed in policy 2021-07"
float_top3: [doc_A (policy-update-2021-07), doc_B (summary), doc_C (forum)]
int8_top3:   [doc_B, doc_A, doc_C]
notes: float score gap between A and B = 0.017; int8 gap = -0.002 (flip). Tokenization identical. Candidate pool identical.
```

meera: That looks like score compression at play. If float gap is already tiny, quant jitter can flip ordering. Bootstrapped CI will tell us if MRR drop is statistically significant.

eval-bot: Bootstrapped CI done: float MRR 0.449 (95% CI [0.441,0.457]), int8 0.440 (95% CI [0.432,0.448]). So CIs overlap but point estimate gap consistent.

zack: Overlap but persistent gap — means small but credible regression. Check ablation A results to see sampler impact.

ci-bot: Job 3400012355 (A) finished. Logs: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/3400012355

irene: Early ablation A: int8 + float-sampler recovers ~0.7% MRR (from -2.6 to -1.9). B (mixed-last-layer) recovers ~0.9%. C (float with int8 clipping) gives -1.8% relative. So both sampler mismatch and quant clipping contribute roughly equally.

meera: Interesting — so partial culprit was the sampler flag mismatch. Good catch. Remaining ~1% is quant math. For longtail, that might be unacceptable depending on product gate. Can we test a cheap mitigation: logit smoothing (scale logits by 1.01 for int8) or add a small temperature in softmax to reduce flips?

zack: Also think about rank-stability postprocess: stable-sort with tiebreaker by doc_id for gaps < 0.005. That prevents nondeterministic-looking flips on tiny gaps. But must be careful not to mask real improvements.

irene: Kicked logit-smoothing ablation: job 3400012388. Also running stable-sort postprocess variant job 3400012399.

ci-bot: Jobs queued: 3400012388, 3400012399.

meera: Meanwhile, add a canary dashboard micro-slice: "low-signal longtail (clicks<=2, query_len<=4)" and a CI assert that candidate_sampler flag parity is required between float and canary runs. We keep missing stratification flags.

zack: Agree. Also record the per-query delta distribution and add to the rollback playbook: if majority of per-query flips are within gap < 0.005, prefer stabilizer+retest; if flips >0.02 or correlate with human click labels, block. Put thresholds in the playbook.

irene: Logit-smoothing early: recovers ~0.6%. Stable-sort recovers ~0.5% but reduces some true uplift cases in other cohorts, so not ideal global fix.

meera: Sounds like best path: (1) fix sampler parity bug and re-run full canary, (2) upstream mitigate quant clipping in PTQ (adjust per-layer clip params), (3) keep logit-smoothing as fallback per-cohort for longtail heavy customers. Opened GT ticket RERANK-7601.

zack: Also add an onboarding checklist item: "verify eval sampler & postprocessing parity" and "run bootstrap CI for low-signal slices".

irene: Will re-run full canary after sampler parity fix and PTQ tweak. ETA ~90m. Thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup:
